execution_path.mechanics: Main select branch maps and selects Paste, then awaits the app handler. The entire terminal-event branch can be suppressed by startup/history/protected-input or thread-switch guards.

Normal explicit paste applies synchronously through chat widget and composer, then syncs popups/recovery state. It flushes pending unbracketed typing and clears paste-burst state. No unconditional three-second explicit-paste delay appears in this path.
A successful ordinary composer edit requests redraw. Immediate frame request enqueues Instant::now on an unbounded MPSC channel; it does not paint inline.

A detached Tokio worker task receives the request, coalesces/clamps deadlines, then emits broadcast only through its Tokio sleep branch. Immediate redraw consequently depends on that task and timer progress. The rate limit is approximately8.33ms/120FPS, not three seconds.
TuiEventStream alternates draw/input poll order; lagged broadcast also maps to Draw. Main-loop guards and awaited handlers can still postpone polling or handling it.

Draw may defer while unbracketed paste capture is active; otherwise it runs pre-draw work and owned/inline transcript rendering. Explicit short paste clears the burst state, so that heuristic is not an established explanation for controlled bracketed-paste lag.

Rendering computes diffs/cursor updates and flushes the backend inside the enclosing synchronized-update closure. A new latency trace must also include return from outer sync_update because backend flush alone does not prove the terminal released the synchronized update or the remote client displayed it.

existing_marker_coverage.first_frame_marks: first_frame_render_begin/done and first_frame_backend_flushed are deduplicated milestones; they do not time later paste redraws.
existing_marker_coverage.handoff: session_prompt_ready and startup_handoff_frame_rendered establish initial configured drawing, not subsequent edit latency.
existing_marker_coverage.dispatch: Existing bounded AppEvent/server samples cover eight events before and eight after handoff within120s; they do not time Paste handling, frame scheduler queue/timer, or active-thread branch awaits.
existing_marker_coverage.unspanned_main_await: app/startup.rs1500 awaits handle_active_thread_event; queued main-loop work before input selection can be outside existing sampled App/server coverage.
existing_marker_coverage.input_boundary: The selected Paste marker would begin after crossterm delivery. It cannot alone partition SSH delivery, terminal-parser/reader delay, main-loop delay before polling, or remote screen presentation.
existing_marker_coverage.clock_qualification: Future poll totals and lifetimes are wall-time observations, not CPU attribution. Host probe and application clocks must not be equated.

minimal_probe_plan.cohort: First four Paste/edit dispatches during a120-second window from TUI loop initialization; classify only static event kinds.
minimal_probe_plan.bounds: At most four input traces and eight active-thread dispatch spans; stop checking clocks once budget/deadline closes. Reuse the existing shared256-span cap; no per-session unbounded logging.
minimal_probe_plan.correlation: Carry a bounded numeric input/request sequence through the real frame request and emitted draw; record first/last request IDs when requests coalesce. Do not infer pairing from unrelated unit broadcasts or insert an extra redraw just to time it.
measurements: Total handle_tui_event and paste-application wall intervals for the selected cohort.
Frame request enqueue-to-receive, requested deadline, actual emit time and due lateness; distinguish immediate and delayed requests.
Bounded actual handle_active_thread_event future spans with static event category to identify waits before the next terminal poll.
minimal_probe_plan.privacy: Numeric sequences/times and static enums only; no pasted text, paths, filenames, cursor content, event Debug output, or payload serialization.
validation_targets: Controlled fake time for immediate/delayed/coalesced frames without changing rate limiting.
First four inputs correlate once with eventual draw or explicit skip/error; expiry and exhausted budget stop clock reads.
Protected input, modal/overlay, owned-screen history, paste burst, resize and render-error behavior remains unchanged.
Compare with reconstructed-screen host probes; any remaining interval outside app selection-to-update-return is upstream/downstream and remains unpartitioned.

optional_extensionless_candidate.candidate: After normalizing a possible pasted path, reject a missing/empty extension before calling image::image_dimensions.
optional_extensionless_candidate.source_basis: normalize_pasted_path accepts one shell token as a relative path. image0.25.9 image_dimensions calls ImageReader::open (File::open), then into_dimensions/into_decoder requires a format. With no extension there is no format and this path cannot succeed; it does not guess content automatically.
optional_extensionless_candidate.expected_effect: Avoid an unnecessary synchronous file open for extensionless ordinary one-token text while preserving currently successful image attachment paths.
limits: Ordinary unquoted two-token probes already fail path normalization before image I/O, so this candidate does not explain or promise to fix their2–4s lag.
Do not reject every unknown extension without separately checking decoding-hook semantics.
No UI performance claim follows from this source observation; any future implementation needs no-file-open and preserved-valid-image tests.

fix_assessment.current_decision: Measure this chain before changing redraw behavior. No unconditional three-second timer was found in the audited explicit-paste/frame limiter path.
not_supported_by_current_evidence: Bypassing frame coalescing/rate limiting or owned-screen/protected-input guards.
Treating long Tokio continuation ages as CPU consumption or proof of a lost wakeup.
Assuming more Tokio workers consistently fixes early input latency.
Claiming input selection or backend flush alone measures physical key arrival or remote screen presentation.
no_changes: No CLI Rust or dependency source changed.
